$comment: Probe corpus for the reconstructed node-side data surface.
Every scenario is executed twice: once through the pinned reference runtime (n8n-workflow@2.9.1 =
the artifact n8n 2.9.4 ships) and once through packages/reconstructed-engine. Results are compared
including thrown errors (name/message/description/context/level), so a wrong value AND a missing
Probe path language: a string is a property read; {"()": [args]} is a call of the value read so far.
The empty-node-name case '$.()' is written as ["$", {"()": ["NodeName"]}].
Provenance of each asserted behaviour is cited per probe group in test/06-data-proxy-golden.test.mjs.

scenarios.name: context-data-and-nodes
scenarios._why: node context data ($('X').context / $input.context) backed by runExecutionData contextData Also carries the $env provider probe: with N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE not set to 'false' the reference throws 'access to env vars denied' on every property read.

scenarios.name: execution-metadata-and-vars
scenarios._why: the additionalKeys half of the sandbox: $execution (id/mode/urls), $vars, the deprecated aliases, and $execution.customData driving execution-metadata. Probes are ORDER-DEPENDENT on purpose: set() then get() must be recorded and replayed in the same sequence. Duplicate probe paths collapse in the golden dict, so each path appears once: getAll is read only after the writes.

scenarios.name: orphan-branch-default
scenarios._why: A node that HAS run data but is not connected to the active node: `$('Code')` must fall back to branchIndex 0, the reference's default for an unconnected source. The `$()` getters compute `getNodeConnectionIndexes(active, node)?.sourceIndex ?? 0`, and a mutation of that default is invisible unless the referenced node has MORE THAN ONE output branch — hence main[0] and main[1] carry different items here.

scenarios.name: pinned-and-disabled-node
scenarios._why: ISSUE-016 follow-up, settled by the oracle instead of by argument: does the data proxy honour `disabled` when it substitutes pinned output? `grep -n disabled packages/workflow/src/workflow-data-proxy.ts` returns NOTHING, while `NodeHelpers.getNodeParametersIssues` (node-helpers.ts:1211) and the execution loop both branch on it. So the proxy layer and the execution layer are allowed to disagree, and the recorded values here are what a port of `$()` must reproduce.

scenarios.name: pinned-upstream-substitutes-input
scenarios._why: workflow-data-proxy.ts:909-926 — getTaskData() falls back to pinDataToTask(), which FABRICATES an ITaskData ({data:{main:[pinData]}, startTime:0, executionTime:0, executionIndex:0, source:[]}) for the previous node when run data is missing, so pinned upstream output reaches $input although NOTHING executed. Two halves are recorded: with a source present the substitution is visible, and with executeData.source absent $input raises 'No execution data available' instead of answering empty. connectionInputData stays empty so the substitution cannot be confused with real input.

scenarios.name: input-placeholder-sourcing-edge
scenarios._why: The reference derives $input's guard from `placeholdersDataInputData`, NOT from the length of connectionInputData: workflow-data-proxy.ts:1061-1079 takes runData[active][runIndex].inputOverride when the ACTIVE node already has run data, and connectionInputData[runIndex].json otherwise, then throws 'No execution data available' when that placeholder object is falsy. A port that only checks `connectionInputData.length === 0` therefore answers where the reference raises — an item with binary and no json is enough to diverge.

scenarios.name: input-placeholder-from-input-override
scenarios._why: Same guard, the other branch: the active node HAS run data carrying inputOverride, so the reference reads the placeholder from there and does not throw even though connectionInputData is empty. Pairs with input-placeholder-sourcing-edge so both sides of `if (!resultData)` are pinned.

scenarios.name: input-placeholder-missing-json
scenarios._why: The divergence candidate for the guard above, found by trying to falsify the port rather than to confirm it: the active node has NO run data and connectionInputData holds an item with `binary` but no `json`. The reference computes placeholders as connectionInputData[runIndex]?.json and throws when that is falsy; a port that guards on `connectionInputData.length === 0` answers instead of raising.

scenarios.name: input-override-ai-tool-placeholder
scenarios._why: Attempt to drive the divergence between the reference guard (`placeholdersDataInputData = runData[active][runIndex].inputOverride[NodeConnectionTypes.AiTool]?.[0]?.itemIndex.json`) and this port's `connectionInputData.length === 0` shortcut: an EMPTY connectionInputData plus an active run whose inputOverride carries an ai_tool placeholder. If the reference answers where the port throws, the shortcut must be replaced by the reference expression; if both throw, the simplification is provably safe today and the scenario records why.

scenarios.name: jmespath-accessor
scenarios._why: $jmesPath / $jmespath (workflow-data-proxy.ts:763-775). The reference imports jmespath as a bare specifier at module scope; this package forbids bare specifiers in src/ (gate 01), so the module is injected and every probe here is graded only where the host can supply it. The arity guard is checked BEFORE the module is touched — that is why the two bad-argument probes below carry expected values even without a runtime. null is accepted by the guard (typeof null === 'object') and the reference spreads it to {}, and arrays are passed to jmespath without the copy — both are pinned here rather than reasoned about.

scenarios.name: luxon-injection
scenarios._why: The luxon seam: workflow-data-proxy.ts:7 imports { DateTime, Duration, Interval, Settings } and the ctor writes Settings.defaultZone = timezone (:90), while the sandbox exposes DateTime.now() (:1535), a SECOND DateTime.now() floored to midnight (:1536) and the three classes as shorthand keys (:1539-1543). Every probe here is chosen to be deterministic so it can be recorded from the reference and replayed offline: fromISO/toISO round-trips print the ambient zone (so skipping the defaultZone write, or using the wrong zone, changes the value), and the class probes prove the keys are real luxon and not stubs. Interval.fromISO and DateTime.fromISO(...).offset are used instead of Interval.parseDuration / offsetNameShort, which this luxon build does not expose — checked against the installed runtime rather than assumed.

deferredProbes.$comment: Symbols the port does NOT implement. They are asserted to raise NotPortedError (loud) rather than return a value (silently wrong). The reference value, when it has one, is recorded by the oracle run. This is the anti-ISSUE-016 pattern: a field or accessor that exists but is inert is worse than one that is missing, because it reads as implemented. NOTE: $env used to live here and was promoted to a real probe — the oracle showed it throwing 'access to env vars denied', and a stub that returns undefined would have looked like a pass. MOVED OUT (2026-09-18): $jmesPath/$jmespath and $now/$today. They are ported now (jmespath and luxon injected), and a wall-clock probe is by construction un-replayable — the recorded $now was 'luxon:2026-09-17T15:41:47.163-04:00', so keeping them here was a latent flake, not coverage. What replaces them is deterministic: the luxon-injection scenario ($now.zoneName, $today.hour, fromISO round-trips that print the ambient zone) plus gate 04's fake-luxon and fake-jmespath tests, which assert the no-injection case raises.
